Hi Hannah —

Appreciate the clear list. Drafted the MAP checklist below and attached a quick token-econ calculator (token-econ-quickcalc.csv) and a working MAP workbook (vitalmesh-map-draft.xlsx) for your team to iterate on. High-level answers and required inputs follow; we'll use these to lock the MAP action items before your procurement sync.

Quick answers (defaults we recommend):
- Canonical tokens/call (model: rw-medium-v1): prompt=110 tokens avg, response=240 tokens avg => ~350 tokens/call baseline.
- KV/prefix cache hit rate: target 30–40% for the first eval run; with prefetching we model 45% as optimistic. Please flag if your ratio of repeated context is higher.
- Batching: continuous batching with a batching factor of 3–6 reduces per-token cost ~12–25% but adds 15–40ms tail depending on burstiness. For latency-sensitive endpoints recommend factor 2–3; for background jobs 5–6.
- Quantization impact: 8-bit quant (~2–3x throughput) reduces GPU cost but may increase small hallucination risk on long-form outputs; tokens/$ uplift modeled in attached CSV.
- Gating criteria (proposed): units/$ <= X where X is computed in the attached sheet (we propose a 20% uplift tolerance vs your target), P95 latency <= 350ms (hosted) or <=450ms (dedicated), eval duration >= 10 business days with traffic >= 50k calls/day or representative sample.

Action items to finalize before procurement:
1) VitalMesh: confirm representative endpoints and attach 48h sample (you mentioned existing snippet).
2) Redwood (Laura): produce a MAP tab with detailed token breakdown per endpoint + cost sensitivity.
3) Redwood (Rishi): confirm rollback thresholds and SLA exceptions for the pilot environment.
4) Joint: schedule a 30m MAP review Monday 10:30am PT.

I'm keeping the MAP light — we'll include a 1-page economics summary for Finance and a technical appendix for your SREs.

Thanks,
RoHan Mehta
Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: token-econ-quickcalc.csv, vitalmesh-map-draft.xlsx

Hi all — adding the concrete cost model assumptions we used to populate the attached sheet. I kept the math conservative so Finance sees a realistic downside.

Assumptions used (short):
- Model: rw-medium-v1 (float32 baseline). We also computed rw-medium-v1-8bit (post-training quant) as a sensitivity.
- Tokens per call: prompt median 100, response median 200 (we modeled 10th/90th percentiles in the sheet). Baseline used 300 tokens/call for the quick calc.
- Batch factor: we simulated batching factor 1, 3, 6. Results: cost/token reduction ~0%, 14%, 22% respectively. Tail latency impact (P95): +8ms, +28ms, +62ms on our Dedicated cluster profile.
- Cache assumptions: no-cache baseline; conservative hit rate 25% (cold-starts/unique prompts). For VitalMesh's stated reuse pattern, we modeled 35% and an optimistic 50% case.
- Prefetch/kv-warm strategy: if VitalMesh can send anchor queries ahead of peak, we model an additional 5–8% effective hit-rate uplift.

Gating thresholds (proposed for MAP signoff):
- Economic gate: End-to-end units/$ must be within +/−20% of target in the conservative model (25% uplift allowed only with joint signoff).
- Performance gate: P95 latency <= 450ms (Dedicated), error rate < 0.5% for the eval period.
- Quality gate: Top-20 prompt evaluation set must show no regression > 3% in acceptability metrics vs baseline model.

Please review the workbook — I left cells for you to enter your traffic mix and weight per endpoint.

-Laura Bennett
Principal Product, Redwood Inference
